title: The Tea Round
logline: Every night for years, a volunteer has pushed a tea trolley along hospital corridors for families who haven't left in days; on the night a patient finally goes home, the same trolley gets pushed a little faster.
human_question: How do you stay useful to people's pain without either flinching from it or being flattened by it?

premise.story: A volunteer's routine of serving tea to relatives waiting outside hospital wards through the night, across ordinary nights and one discharge.
premise.place: Hospital corridors and benches at night, the grounds just outside a ward.
premise.experience: Long, quiet hours of small kindness, and the sudden lift when someone finally goes home.

concept_links.why: Compassion toward the suffering and gladness at another's good fortune are separate responses that take turns, each needing a specific person actually in view [C027-M:L21; C027-P:L47].
The same shift from wishing someone's pain to end toward gladness at their good fortune, without dwelling permanently in either [C095-P4:L39].
Years of steady, unglamorous giving whose return is not the visible point of the act [C012-M:L22].

what_camera_could_observe: Night corridors and benches, the tea trolley on its round
On another night, a discharge: hugs, relief, the volunteer's visible gladness
The volunteer's own account of years of doing this
what_must_be_real: Explicit, informed consent from every patient and relative shown. No identifying detail of anyone's medical condition without consent.

possible_arc.turn: A longer, harder wait for one particular family.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever actually happens to that family, whether the news is good or not.

position_hint: closing candidate: hands the group off to the next stage's concern with the body's fragility, seen here in the sick and those keeping vigil through the night

requirements: Hospital administration approval for filming in patient-adjacent areas
